texts.facts: AWARD "The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner." 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case as per the investigation by the Police officials concerned are that on 06.07.2018 concerned police officials and found injured / claimant and her mother at Batra Hospital. They told the police officials that driver of TSR / Offending vehicle is known to them and at that time they do not want any police complaint. As such DD No. 15PP was kept pending. Later on Gunja vs . Salman & Ors, on 10 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111842070/ 1 such minor injured / claimant in presence of her mother Asha at their home stated that she's study at Government School, Kali Building, Dakshin Puri in 8 th Class. That on 05.07.2018 she along with her friends Kajal, Kumkum, Pooja, Komal and Rekha in the morning about 07:00 AM were going in the Auto of Salman bearing no. HR-38-T-1042 to Kalkaji Temple. When they were coming back from Kalkaji Temple than about 08:15 AM at Maa Anandmai Marg, Near Petrol Pump, One water tanker was parked on the side of the road. There such TSR heated from behind with force and such MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 2 of 25 rpt victim along with her friends were already stating to R1 to drive the vehicle slowly but he was driving at a fast speed in a rash and negligent manner and lost control. As a result, due to such collusion, leg of injured came out of the Auto and struck between auto and such vehicle / tanker. Resultantly she received injury. Such auto driver was known to them as he used to take them to school also, thus he took her Batra Hospital for medical treatment. Such R1 further undertook and assured to bear the medical expense of injured. But later refused to do so. Accordingly it is stated by Claimant side that they want to proceed on merit as such driver even left his house. 3. Accordingly the FIR in question u/s 279/337 IPC was registered. Further after investigation, chargesheet u/s 279/338 was filed apart from various offence under the MV Act. Further more, present DAR is also filed by the concerned police official. 4. In this case, inter alia there was no third party insurance of such offending vehicle. 5. Further, Medical Board of Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, New Delhi sent disability report dated 03.10.2022 noticing 42% permanent disability in relation to right lower limb. 6. Further, as per record, initially R-1 / driver appeared. But later on he neither filed any reply nor contested the present case. Further as per record, R2/registered owner was not traceable. 7. It may be further noted that my Ld. Predecessor MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 3 of 25 rpt issued show cause notice to the Respondent to deposit FDR as security of Rs. 03 Lakhs, in view of MACT Rules / Directions of Hon'ble Higher Courts. But no such security deposited. 8. Further as per record even directions were issued to Ld. Ilaka MM for auction of the offending vehicle and deposit the sale proceedings in this Tribunal but as per the latest report of Ld. Ilaka MM such auction could not be carried out so far as there was some administrative issue, district nazir, Government of NCT of Delhi and concerned selling agency relating to agreement and its renewal etc. 9. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 11.01.2019 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. Whether the injured baby Gunja suffered injuries in the road accident on 05.07.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR 38 T 1042 (TSR) being driven by respondent no.1/driver, owned by respondent no.2/owner? OPP. Gunja vs . Salman & Ors, on 10 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111842070/ 2 2. Whether the injured to entitle to any compensation, if so to what extent and from whom? 3. Relief. 10. Further, as per record, injured/petitioner examined herself as PW-1. Such PW-1 tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/X. She relied upon various documents including medical bills, DAR, Aadhaar Card and Disability certificate as Ex. PW-1/A till Ex. PW-1/D. 11. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 17. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 5 of 25 rpt it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. , it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 23. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 7 of 25 rpt Gunja vs . Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 23.1. MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 8 of 25 rpt 23.5. 23.6. Salman & Anr. Page No. 9 of 25 rpt (iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,that is, the permanent disability suffered by the person. In Judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as "M. R. Krishna Murthi vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. on 5 March, 2019, (2020) 15 SCC 493: (2020) 4 SCC (Crl.) 84: 2019 SCC Online SC 315 , after dealing with various case laws relating to injury matters and death cases in case of students, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows: "24. From the conjoint reading of the aforesaid judgments, inter alia, following principles can be culled out which would be relevant for deciding the instant appeal: 24.1 In those cases where the victim of the accident is not an earning person but a student, while assessing the compensation for loss of future earning, the focus of the examination would be the career prospect and the likely earning of such a person in future. For example, where the claimant is pursuing a particular professional course, the poseer would be: what would have been his income had he joined a service commensurating with the said course. That can be the future earning. 24.2 There may be cases where the victim is not, at that stage, MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. In such a case, future career would depend upon multiple factors like the family background, choice/interest of the complainant to pursue a particular career, facilities available to him/her for adopting such a career, the favourable surrounding circumstances to see which would have enabled the claimant to successfully pick up the said career etc. In case, career is a particular profession, the future earning Gunja vs . It is further argued by counsel for claimant that she suffered permanent disability and a disability certificate dt. 03.10.2022 noticing 42% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb, Ex. The nature of injuries are grievous and MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 13 of 25 rpt petitioner suffered 42% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb. (v) Loss of income : Notional Rs.50,000/- Compensation towards loss of study. MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 14 of 25 rpt (iii) Loss of amenities of life : The Rs. 20,000/- petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and suffered 42 % permanent physical impairment in relation to left lower limb. 39. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., MAC Appeal no. 433/2013, decided on 18.10.2022 it was noted regarding rate of interest: "25 to evaluate the submission made by counsel for the applicants, it is imperative to examine the guiding principles for the grant of interest. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. The rate of interest must be just and reasonable depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case and taking all relevant factors including inflation, change of economy, policy being adopted by Reserve Bank of India from time to time, how long the case is pending, permanent injuries suffered by the victim, enormity of suffering, loss of future income, loss of enjoyment of life etc. into consideration. Neither Sec. 34 CPC nor Sec. 4-A(3) of Workmen's Compensation Act are applicable in the MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. The courts have awarded the interest at different rates depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case. Therefore, in my opinion, there cannot be any hard and fast rule in awarding interest and the award of interest is solely on the discretion of Gunja vs . Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 41. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs. 10,18,755/- with simple interest at the rate of 9% p.a. for the period as noted above. LIABILITY:- 42. Further in the case of "Naveen Kumar vs. Vijay Kumar ((2018) 3 SCC 1), which is a three judges Bench judgment that too of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India where the law is well clarified for the purpose of present proceeding even after MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 17 of 25 rpt transferring/selling his vehicle to another person when his name is continued to be reflected in the record of registering authority as owner, such registered owner would continue to be treated as owner under MV Act and would not stand absolved of his liability as owner under the Act. 45. Accordingly, it is held that the driver / R-1 as well as registered owner / R-2 are jointly and severally liable to pay such compensation/award amount of Rs. 10,18,755/- with simple interest @ 9% p.a., as directed above. 46. 47. This court is in receipt of the orders dated 07.12.2018 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in FAO no. 842/2003 titled as Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. Vs. Jaibir Singh & Ors whereby the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has formulated MACAD(Motor Accident Claims Annunity Deposit Scheme) which has been made effective from 01.01.2019. The said orders dated 07.12.2018 also mentions that 21 banks including State Bank of India is one of such banks which are to adhere to MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 18 of 25 rpt MACAD. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Gunja vs . Another issue which is to be decided is out of such Award amount, how much is to be released at present and how much is to kept in the form of FDR for future financial used of the petitioner. 49. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. However, in such cases, the Tribunal shall make sure that the amount is actually spent for the purpose and the demand is not a ruse to withdraw money. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 19 of 25 rpt purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons. It needs to be clarified that the MACT No. 980/18 Gunja v. Salman & Anr. Page No. 20 of 25 rpt above guidelines were issued by this Court only to safeguard the interests of the claimants, particularly the minors, illiterates and others whose amounts are sought to be withdrawn on some fictitious grounds.
